P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title and no setter notes exist to read back, so P1a is N/A. The rep opened cold with rapport — 'how long have you been following Trevor and how well do you know kettlebells?' — and never set the four-part frame or asked for frame agreement. He did run the open question: 'So what brought you people? How can we actually help?'

P2.evidence: Work was covered properly ('what you do for like on a day to day basis?' plus 'you probably sit a lot too, yeah?'). Training week and diet were both asked directly ('what do you do currently in terms of working out? Are you following any program whatsoever?' and 'about nutrition... Are you following any specific diet?'). Age and height were never asked; weight only surfaced because the prospect volunteered '180 and 184' in response to a fat-loss question. Health conditions were never asked — high cholesterol was volunteered. Injuries were volunteered, though the rep did probe duration ('This was when?' / 'And you still feel it?'), hence partial. Sleep, daily energy, and results from current training were never touched.

P3.evidence: Strong on the middle of the phase: 'having a structure and actually fixing up those problems, that would be the main goal for you?', 'What you're going to do with all the strength that you will gain? What do you need it for?', and the bridge 'in your mind, Kareem, what's the biggest reason you want to actually make this change right now?' The deep end was left on the table — 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked even though a 14-month-old son was on the table from minute one, and there was no explicit reflect-back of the form 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about X.' The closest reflect-back was the pillar-transition summary at 00:26:32.

P4.evidence: Best-run phase. 'So apart from this body weight training, you haven't tried anything to actually fix those injuries and stuff?' surfaced the failed PTs and the Kinstretch program, and 'what's kept you from actually making it happen for all those years?' produced the prospect naming his own gap — no structure, no accountability, a self-serve program with nobody holding him to it. The rep reinforced it with the tech-guy structure pattern. He never ran the explicit 'the information isn't the problem' line.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was essentially skipped. The prospect himself started to open the door — 'Because if I don't have this, like, in 10-20 years...' — and the rep redirected to 'What answer did you come up with when you asked yourself?' rather than running the two-year question. No 'willing to settle for that', no 'why not'. The line-in-the-sand move did land, delivered as a statement: 'So you say enough is enough. You drew a line in the sand and you want to commit to this.'

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions were run cleanly before any price was mentioned: 'if you had the right training, the right nutrition, and guidance and accountability from Trevor built around your life, do you agree that you would get to your goals getting stronger, pain-free...?' and 'if we can figure out all the logistical details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work?' — answered '100%'. Only then did he move to the investment.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and a payment link was put in the chat, so the phase applies, but not one of the four steps was completed before hanging up. Payment was deferred to a second meeting ('Can we meet, like, at 5 p.m.?'), the Trevor call was only promised ('get you on the call with Trevor, even this week'), and nothing was said about the agreement, the welcome email, Skool or the onboarding questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: Ran the opening isolation move well — 'let's take money out of the equation for a second. Do you still personally feel that this can get you to the goals?' — and the obstacles probe, 'when you talk to her, what do you feel maybe potential obstacles for her'. Then abandoned the play: never asked whether there is any reason she would not want him stronger and out of pain, never asked whether this genuinely needs her input or is permission to bet on himself, never used the 'this isn't a joint decision like buying a house' frame, and never offered the deposit-with-refund fallback. Instead pivoted to a logistics reframe and booked a payment call, which worked but left the wife conversation unresolved.

Nanny costs and household budget pressure were raised. The rep used the core reframe almost verbatim — 'it's, like, not a, should I do it? It's more of a, how' — but ran none of the rest: no 'finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%' isolation, no offer to break the payment up, no permission question about an honest financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture questions (cash on hand, monthly surplus, number of cards, available credit, used vs available, investments). The only financial question asked was 'cash or credit'.

notes: Discovery and commitment were genuinely strong — P4 and P6 are the model of how this should run, and he earned a yes before naming a price. The two structural gaps are P5, which was skipped almost entirely when the prospect had already opened the door to it, and P11, where a live buyer with a link in the chat was allowed off the call with zero onboarding steps completed. Also: when asked point-blank 'is there like a monthly plan?', the answer was 'put it on a credit card' — the playbook's own break-it-up option was never surfaced.
